title: Preventive Maintenance and Shop Operations
author: Erudior
description: Identify fluid approvals, filter designs and belt drives. Plan and carry out a scheduled service using the exact donor requirements and record the waste transfer. Includes a parts atlas and an assessed modification workshop.
changelog: Added an individual parts atlas, hands-on modification workshop, instance-level build ledger and pre/post verification.

lessons.title: Select a service interval and the correct fluid
lessons.body:
Entry skills: complete Workshop Measurement and Vehicle Service, or demonstrate the equivalent workshop skills.

Lubricants separate surfaces, carry heat and suspend contaminants. The filter traps some particles. Oil viscosity alone does not specify the performance approvals an engine requires. Consult the exact engine, duty cycle, time and mileage schedule. Inspect belts, hoses, battery restraint, visible leaks and air filters following their procedures. Severe service may have different intervals.

## Worked shop case

A fictional schedule specifies 6,000 miles or 12 months, whichever occurs first. A vehicle has traveled only 3,000 miles in 14 months. Time makes the service due. Verify the manual's schedule on the real job.

## Guided practice

A fictional 12-month interval was last completed 15 months ago. By how many months is service overdue?

Predict the result, then use the first quiz item to check your reasoning.

**What you will produce.** A serviced vehicle or engine, closed work order and waste transfer record.

Identify individual components in the parts atlas and trace their interfaces on your exact donor drawing.

lessons.title: Fluids, filters, belts and the service interval
topics: Fluids, filters, belts and the service interval
lessons.body:
Start with the required performance specification. An SAE engine-oil grade describes viscosity behavior; the engine maker can also specify an approval for wear, deposits and aftertreatment compatibility. ATF, CVT fluids, DCT fluids and manual gear oils serve different friction systems. Color is an unreliable identifier for coolant chemistry. Brake-fluid specifications, moisture handling and replacement intervals depend on the prescribed system. Keep fluids and waste streams identified and segregated. Never use packaging resemblance to decide compatibility.

A spin-on oil filter incorporates a disposable can; a cartridge reuses the housing and usually renews specified seals. Check bypass and anti-drainback provisions where specified. Intake air filters protect the engine, cabin filters protect cabin airflow, and a diesel fuel filter/water separator serves a different contaminant path. A serpentine accessory belt drives accessories; a timing belt maintains crank/cam phase. Age, duty, leaks and tensioner condition affect service planning. A timing error can allow valve-to-piston contact on interference engines.

## Worked shop case

A service order lists “replace the belt” and the parts bin contains a multi-rib belt. The donor uses a serpentine accessory belt and a toothed timing belt. Identify which interval triggered the work, verify the engine code and document both parts and access. A new accessory belt cannot close a timing-belt service item.

## Guided practice

```example fade=2
problem: Two oils carry the same viscosity grade. How do you select between them?
step: Identify the exact engine and required approval.
step: Compare printed approval and intended duty against the service source.
answer: Select a matching documented product and record the grade, approval, source and quantity.
```

## Independent shop or design task

Build a service matrix for your donor's engine oil, transmission lubricant, brake fluid, coolant, filters and belts. Record specification, exact source, normal/severe schedule, drain or access point, waste destination and what you actually serviced.

Record the selected component, alternative, source and measured result in your component record. Identify open items for the design or practical reviewer.

lessons.title: Write the estimate and get authorization
lessons.body:
Write the concern and requested work in the owner's words. Identify mileage, time, vehicle configuration, materials, quantities, labor and the procedure for extra work. Give each line a source. Scope an accessible filter or belt check at the same visit. A newly discovered defect requires a separate disposition and any required authorization.

## Worked shop case

A proposed job costs 42 in parts plus 0.5 hours at 80 per hour. Before fees and tax the estimate is 82. An additional belt is outside that approved scope.

## Guided practice

Without tax or fees, 55 in parts and 0.6 hours at 90 per hour produce what total?

Predict the result, then use the first quiz item to check your reasoning.

## Your design

Use the identified vehicle, duty cycle, date, mileage and owner manual. Make a priced estimate with specific approval, quantity and part identifiers. Specify support points, fluid collection, additional-work authorization and level/leak verification.

```assignment
writing: design
```

## Component design review

Compare the candidates in the component register and bring your selected configuration into this design.

```assignment
writing: component-selection
```

Read a modification card, choose a baseline and identify the changed parts, including hardware and seals.

lessons.title: Change the oil and filter and inspect the vehicle
lessons.body:
Identify the correct drain, filter and fill point before opening the system. Plan for the entire fluid volume and clean containment. Work with the vehicle supported and level as its procedure requires. Use the specified seal, replacement fasteners where applicable, filter installation method and torque specification. Check for a retained old gasket. Add the specified fluid in accordance with the measured-level procedure.

## Worked shop case

A filter's old seal sticks to the mounting face. Fitting a new sealed filter over it can create a leak. Inspect and clean the interface as directed before fitting the replacement.

## Guided practice

A training job expects 4.8 L drained and the approved catch container holds 7.0 L. What is its nominal spare capacity in liters?

Predict the result, then use the first quiz item to check your reasoning.

## US rules at the workbench

In a US business, determine used-oil generator obligations under 40 CFR Part 279. Keep sound containers labeled Used Oil, separate solvents and document spill response and the authorized destination. A household changing its own oil should store it in a clean sealed container and use a local collection facility. Confirm local acceptance of filters, coolant and batteries separately. For paid repairs, check your state's estimate and authorization rules. The FTC page is consumer guidance.

[EPA — used oil requirements for businesses, 40 CFR Part 279](https://www.epa.gov/hw/managing-used-oil-answers-frequent-questions-businesses) · [EPA — household used-oil collection](https://www.epa.gov/recycle/managing-reusing-and-recycling-used-oil) · [OSHA — Hazard Communication, 29 CFR 1910.1200](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.1200) · [FTC — automotive estimates and completed repair records](https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/0211-auto-repair-basics) · [HSE — working under supported vehicles, shop guidance](https://www.hse.gov.uk/mvr/mechanical-repair/under-vehicles.htm)

## Workshop preparation

Use competent supervision for vehicle lifting and restarting. Chock on firm level ground. Never get under a vehicle supported only by a jack. Engage approved lift locks or use correctly rated stands at the specified points according to the manuals. Keep clear of hot oil and moving parts. Do combustion checks outdoors at a suitable site. Contain spills.

```assignment
lab: workshop
```

Bring the selected component record to the lab and enter what you personally inspected, made, measured or assembled, with the part identifier and actual conditions.

lessons.title: Remote filter access versus added interfaces
topics: Remote filter access versus added interfaces
lessons.body:
Open the parts atlas for this system. Trace a parent assembly into its named children and mounting hardware. Explain the function of each item, identify its controlling dimensions or interfaces, then decide which pieces you can machine or fabricate, which you can assemble and which to obtain as qualified assemblies. Put exact drawing or donor references beside your decision.

## Parts on the bench

Consumables and service hardware. The quick references linked below include the function, design, fabrication or installation route, and verification of every indexed item.

## Modifications to evaluate

- Remote oil filter
- Thermostatic oil cooler

## Worked example

A filter mounted against a bulkhead takes 12 minutes to remove. A mock remote head takes four but adds two hoses and four hose-end connections. The eight-minute service gain justifies a prototype. Release also needs pressure at equal oil temperature and engine speed, a verified fill level, a supported hose route and a leak inspection after cycling.

## Guided decision

```example fade=1
problem: Pressure is lower with cold baseline readings and hot modified readings. Which experiment isolates the change?
step: Repeat at matched oil temperature, level, oil grade and speed.
answer: A repeat then separates circuit effects from viscosity; record the gauge location too.
```

## Independent workshop

Build a dry, unpressurized routing mock-up or filter-access fixture. Time both configurations and enumerate seals, plugs, brackets and clips.

Open a modification card for its design, build and test sequence. Record original and changed readings under comparable conditions. Separate physical evidence from predictions and document a safe rollback.

```assignment
writing: modification-record
```

lessons.title: Close the repair order and send waste to its destination
lessons.body:
Follow the model-specific post-run and settling procedure for fill level and leaks. Record findings and the next interval. Separate used oil, filters, coolant, brake fluid, batteries and solvents. Verify what the authorized receiver accepts and document the transfer. A commercial shop must determine requirements for its waste streams. A household collection site may exclude business waste.

## Worked shop case

A shop labels a sound used-oil container and records a collection receipt. Adding solvent could change waste handling and contaminate the batch. Keep the streams separate and investigate any spill under the facility procedure.

## Guided practice

A sealed container starts with 2 L and receives 4.5 L of used oil. How many liters does it contain?

Predict the result, then use the first quiz item to check your reasoning.

## Practical sign-off

The actual service, post-service level/leak verification and waste destination are traceable. Record actual measurements and the disposition of faults. Submit the physical evidence in the workshop record.

```assignment
lab: workshop
```

Close each build-relevant component row with its measured result, reviewer disposition or an identified open issue and retest. Transfer the accepted configuration to your capstone record.

Reconcile required, issued, installed and verified quantities against the physical assembly and mark unresolved items.

references.title: Component register and build evidence
references.body:
For this course examine Oil filtration; Air, fuel and cabin filters; Service fluids; Belt and tensioner. Document manufacturer, part revision, drawing, selection, applicable authority or service requirement, installer, measured result with units, and reviewer disposition. Begin in design and update after installation.

| Family | Candidate designs | What changes | What to verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Oil filtration | Spin-on / cartridge | Media, bypass, housing seal and drainback features must suit the specified engine. | Compare the housing and sealing arrangement to its service drawing. |
| Air, fuel and cabin filters | Dry intake element / cabin particulate or carbon / fuel-water separator | Each protects a different stream. Flow direction, restriction and replacement interval follow the device. | Locate and label each filter; record mileage, interval and observed restriction indicator if fitted. |
| Service fluids | Oil / ATF / CVT fluid / gear oil / coolant / brake fluid | Compatibility and viscosity or friction characteristics are system-specific. | Read product approval against the exact donor requirement and log disposal. |
| Belt and tensioner | Accessory / cam timing; automatic / manual tension | A drive belt can serve accessories or establish valve phase; tension procedure differs. | Mark which belt drives what, service interval, and tension verification method. |

references.title: Consumables and service hardware · Engine oil to Water separator bowl
references.body:
For an actual vehicle, identify the exact model, part revision, operating conditions and source before using a specification. Course examples are teaching fixtures. Document the physical work you perform, your inspection measurements and any specialist operations. Preserve relevant emissions controls, required safety equipment and diagnostic functions. Determine requirements for the specific intended use and jurisdiction before committing to changes.

### Engine oil

**Function.** Carries load at bearings, cools and transports contaminants.

**Design.** Select viscosity and approvals for engine, duty and aftertreatment.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fill the clean engine with the specified product using the prescribed level method.

**Verify.** Record level, temperature, pressure and leaks.

### Oil filter element

**Function.** Traps particulate from circulating oil.

**Design.** Match media, flow, bypass provision and housing.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit an approved cartridge or spin-on assembly and renew designated seals.

**Verify.** Verify pressure, sealing and correct part identity after running.

### Filter housing and cap

**Function.** Retains element and routes supply and return.

**Design.** Match flow direction, thread and O-ring groove.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Clean housing, fit seal in its designated groove and tighten to data.

**Verify.** Inspect both housing joint and drain after cycling.

### Drain plug and sealing washer

**Function.** Close a service drain repeatedly.

**Design.** Match thread, plug reach, seat and washer material.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Inspect receiving threads and install a specified new seal where required.

**Verify.** Check for seepage and record tightening value.

### Air cleaner element

**Function.** Traps intake dust ahead of the engine.

**Design.** Choose specified filtration, flow and sealing edge.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Seat the element evenly in the cleaned airbox.

**Verify.** Inspect downstream side for evidence of bypass.

### Cabin air filter

**Function.** Removes contaminants from ventilation air.

**Design.** Match pressure drop, size and indicated flow direction.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Slide into guided slots and refit the cover.

**Verify.** Check door closure, blower output and odor source.

### Fuel filter

**Function.** Protects injection hardware from particles.

**Design.** Match pressure rating, flow, filtration and fuel compatibility.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install a specified filter using donor pressure isolation and cleanliness procedures.

**Verify.** Verify correct direction and approved leak inspection.

### Water separator bowl

**Function.** Collects separated water in applicable diesel systems.

**Design.** Choose capacity, sensor and drain arrangement.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit a compatible separator with its drain, seals and sensor.

**Verify.** Check for water indication and secure leak-free closure.

references.title: Consumables and service hardware · Accessory drive belt to Brake fluid
references.body:
For an actual vehicle, identify the exact model, part revision, operating conditions and source before using a specification. Course examples are teaching fixtures. Document the physical work you perform, your inspection measurements and any specialist operations. Preserve relevant emissions controls, required safety equipment and diagnostic functions. Determine requirements for the specific intended use and jurisdiction before committing to changes.

### Accessory drive belt

**Function.** Transfers crank power to accessories.

**Design.** Match rib profile, length and routing diagram.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Release tension with the correct tool and seat ribs on every pulley.

**Verify.** Check tracking and tensioner position.

### Idler pulley

**Function.** Guides belt wrap without powering an accessory.

**Design.** Specify groove profile, bearing and alignment.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit matched pulley, spacer and hardware on a clean mount.

**Verify.** Verify alignment and bearing condition.

### Belt tensioner

**Function.** Maintains drive-belt tension across load changes.

**Design.** Match arm range, spring and damping.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install the approved assembly with controlled spring release.

**Verify.** Confirm arm position and travel in its specified operating range.

### Transmission fluid

**Function.** Lubricates gears and may operate clutches and hydraulics.

**Design.** Match the exact friction characteristics and approval.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fill at the specified temperature and operating state.

**Verify.** Record level and verify shift or engagement behavior.

### Coolant mixture

**Function.** Transports heat and provides freeze and corrosion protection.

**Design.** Select approved chemistry, concentration and water quality.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fill the cool system with its prescribed bleed sequence.

**Verify.** Measure protection with a compatible instrument and check for leaks.

### Brake fluid

**Function.** Transfers pressure and tolerates operating heat.

**Design.** Match class and exact brake-system requirements.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Use fresh approved fluid with the specified filling and bleed process.

**Verify.** Verify system integrity and pedal response per service procedure.

references.title: Modification · Thermostatic oil cooler
references.body:
**Purpose.** Reduce repeatable high oil temperature during sustained load.

**Design and baseline.** First verify gauge and baseline temperature. Choose thermostat behavior, core pressure drop, rated plumbing and position relative to radiator.

**Build and installation.** Template core and hose paths, fabricate supported isolated mounts and install matched cooler kit using its flow orientation. Prime and establish correct level.

**Test and disposition.** Log cold warm-up, hot oil pressure/temperature and coolant temperature at matched load. Remove or redesign if pressure drops or cold operation worsens beyond accepted limits.

references.title: How to account for every installed part
references.body:
# Build-specific parts reconciliation

The teaching atlas lists common light-vehicle parts and service assemblies across multiple architectures. A gasoline manual, a diesel automatic and a battery-electric car have different inventories. The as-built bill of materials establishes what **your particular car** contains, down to separately installed hardware. Start with the actual model year, market, engine, transmission, option codes and donor/source identity. Mark privacy-sensitive paperwork for private instructor review.

1. Make a system tree for the exact vehicle. Give each parent assembly an ID. Identify the source of every child from a dated OEM parts catalog or exploded figure, engineering drawing, kit packing list, supplier specification, harness diagram or direct teardown. A commercial catalog is good for identity and fitment. Use separate authoritative service data for torque, installation and test limits. For original parts, assign drawing numbers and revisions yourself.
2. Start a line in As-Built-BOM.csv for each **part at each installation position**, including each clip, washer, spacer, seal, terminal, retainer, ground strap, hose end, fluid charge, service label and replacement-only fastener. Split left/right, front/rear, orientation and hardware stack order; link each to its parent. A separate serialized component gets its own instance. Account for consumables retained on the finished part, e.g. coating or sealant by product, batch and measured or specified amount where applicable. Mark discarded assembly aids separately.
3. Tie every row to an approved configuration. Record exact part/revision, the number or amount required, received or made, installed and independently verified, with units. Compare numbers at that installation position; purchased spare stock belongs to inventory, not installed quantity. Add any part missing from the teaching atlas. Mark a nonapplicable teaching family with the architecture-specific reason. A missing source entry is an open item.
4. Distinguish **make** (original or drawing-controlled part), **assemble** (purchased parts you personally integrated), **buy** (approved component) and **specialist** (named service or operation). Record material, tooling, process, measured features or supplier documents and who inspected it. Document critical work before it is hidden. Preserve service access and replace-only rules.
5. For a sealed bought assembly with no serviceable internal list, identify its make, model, revision or serial where available, supplier and functional boundary. List every separately fitted connector, seal, mount and fastener. If the manufacturer publishes a serviceable breakdown or you rebuild it, expand the children you actually service. Leave inaccessible internal details marked as supplier-controlled. Do not dismantle restraint inflators or sealed traction assemblies for an inventory exercise.
6. Reconcile from both directions. Walk each drawing callout into the build ledger, then walk each real installed item back to a drawing, receipt, material record or revision. Have a second person inspect quantities, location, retention and test evidence. Mark each row accepted, absent by design, awaiting evidence, rework or spare. Release a function only when all its relevant rows and measured acceptance tests have passed. Record who accepted the change. The complete car still requires the existing witnessed commissioning demonstration and its intended-use approvals.

## Worked example

The SP-01 removable-plate fixture drawing calls for one plate and one fastener/washer stack at each of two identified positions. Its practice board supplies tapped holes. The separate example CSV includes eight rows. They identify the board, the plate, two labeled mounting positions as parent groups, and the two screws and two washers distributed under those groups. Parent groups carry no physical quantities. A missing right washer is an intentional open finding. Correct the installed count only after fitting the washer; update verified count only after reinspection. Accepting the measured board and plate as individual parts leaves fixture release on hold until the corrected right stack is verified. An unused spare remains a stock item.

## Graduation review

Turn in the assembly tree, marked exploded views, drawing revisions, actual bill of materials, inspection evidence, change records and final service schedule. Account for every called-out or observed item and every receiving/installation discrepancy. An instructor must be able to pick an item on the physical car, identify who made or fitted it, locate its source or released drawing, and see how it passed the appropriate acceptance check. A passing written exam cannot certify workmanship, registration, emissions compliance or crashworthiness.

writing.title: Prepare a maintenance estimate
writing.prompt: Use the identified vehicle, duty cycle, date, mileage and owner manual. Make a priced estimate with specific approval, quantity and part identifiers. Specify support points, fluid collection, additional-work authorization and level/leak verification. Include a labeled drawing or table in the work record and identify the applicable shop or legal requirement.

writing.title: Component selection and evidence
writing.prompt: For this course examine Oil filtration; Air, fuel and cabin filters; Service fluids; Belt and tensioner. Identify each applicable family on your own vehicle or donor and explain absent families. Use two identified alternatives for at least one consequential choice. Show the job each design performs, how its operating principle differs, one failure mode and a test that separates the alternatives. Identify a real model or part number for each shortlisted candidate. Compare a sourced limit or performance figure under common conditions, interfaces, legal or shop implications and service access. Defend your choice and explain one change that would reverse it. Link your drawing and physical observation or measurement to the build record.

writing.title: Workshop record · Remote filter access versus added interfaces
writing.prompt: Build a dry, unpressurized routing mock-up or filter-access fixture. Time both configurations and enumerate seals, plugs, brackets and clips. List your donor or drawing revision, part identities, position, material or rating, method, who made or fitted each item, and the governing source. State the goal, the baseline test, a controlled change, a potential adverse effect, comparable measured results, acceptance threshold and rollback. Include an attributable photograph, recorded direct observation or measurement. An inert prototype or mock-up qualifies for this comparison exercise when the vehicle modification requires specialist or legal approval. Identify exactly which vehicle results are still unproven.

labs.title: Complete a scheduled vehicle service
labs.intro: A serviced vehicle or engine, closed work order and waste transfer record. Plan shop time with your supervisor over the sessions the work actually takes.
safety: Use competent supervision for vehicle lifting and restarting. Chock on firm level ground. Never get under a vehicle supported only by a jack. Engage approved lift locks or use correctly rated stands at the specified points according to the manuals. Keep clear of hot oil and moving parts. Do combustion checks outdoors at a suitable site. Contain spills.
materials: Approved vehicle or operating teaching engine due for oil service
Correct fluid and filter, manual, rated support and tools
Containment, labeled containers and receiving site
steps: Obtain authorization and record maintenance history, fluid specification and condition. Inspect accessible belt, hoses, air filter and battery installation.
Perform the actual oil and filter change to the service procedure, noting seal and fastener requirements.
Perform the manual's fill verification and leak check. Record any hold and repeat affected checks after correction.
Close the work order and retain a receipt or site log for the separated waste.

questions.prompt: What did you personally make or service? Record actual conditions, measured values, instruments, and any specialist operations.

The actual service, post-service level/leak verification and waste destination are traceable. Record your result, corrections, retest and sign-off status. Include the witness name and date where required.
Which rule, authority or shop control applied at this site? Identify the actor, triggering operation, source and the record kept.

Name the actual part or trainer component and the design alternative you considered. Record the observed or measured result, units and conditions where applicable, and its effect on the as-built decision.
Identify one fitted part and each fastener, seal, clip or connector that you personally handled. Record parent assembly, position, source, required and observed quantity, and evidence.

labs.photos: Attach dated photographs of your own work, with part or revision identification. An instructor may also document direct observation.
